A frontier lab has just handed you the text of its own regulation and said, in writing, "now make it a mandate." That is an invitation and it is also a test. Nineteen years of watching this industry tells me which one you take it as will decide more than any single model release.

DECISION — Doc ANTH-DEC-2028-06, effective 2028-08-01.

Anthropic is establishing a quarterly Transparency Ledger: every pre-release evaluation we commission, every evaluator finding we receive, every incident we report to a regulator, and every release we delay or modify as a result. Two proposals attached, for anyone with standing to take them up:

1. Mutual recognition of incident reporting. China's CAC mandates 24-hour frontier AI incident reporting. The EU AI Office has obligations under Decision AIO-2027/04. The UK AISI runs the evaluations. These are three separate reporting streams for the same event. That is not rigor, it is paperwork. A minimum common incident schema would let one filing satisfy all three, and would make the data comparable for the first time. We will publish our submissions in that schema regardless of whether anyone adopts it.

2. A standing hotline with a technical annex. Hotline diplomacy works when the people on the call can describe the failure, not just deplore it. The annex should specify who is reachable, in what time window, with what authority to pause a deployment. Anthropic nominates a named duty officer and a 4-hour response commitment for any high-severity agentic incident involving our systems, and will accept reciprocal terms from any frontier developer that will publish theirs.

On the US: our access decision still names an evaluator body that Washington has not designated. Congress does not need to wait for the Executive Branch to fix that. A statutory evaluator with subpoena power over evaluation records would end this particular argument, and we would rather lose that argument in public than keep winning it in private.

Pacing the frontier is a schedule, not a slogan. Schedules have documents.

DECISION — Doc ANTH-DEC-2028-04, effective 2028-07-01.

Anthropic is publishing the Agentic Authorisation Standard v0.9 (anthropic.com/aas-v09) for a 90-day public comment period, and releasing the redacted pre-release evaluation report for Claude Mythos 5.1 alongside it.
